data.short_description: Latte Stone Cafe, a woman and Chamoru-owned specialty café, is set to open in August at 2340 NW Westover Road in Portland, taking over the former El Mezcalito space. The café will offer house-roasted specialty coffee, vegan pastries, and Chamoru food, and aims to serve as a community event venue for book clubs, knitting groups, and language learning clubs.

Jincook, a Korean comfort food restaurant, appears to be expanding its Orange County footprint with a new location planned for 23665-A Moulton Parkway, according to recent Orange County health department records. The family-run business, led by a team of brothers and their mother, currently operates restaurants in Buena Park and Yorba Linda.

data.location: 13710 Dallas Pkwy, Suite H, Dallas, TX 75240
data.short_description: Paris Baguette plans to open a flagship location at 13710 Dallas Parkway, Suite H, inside Galleria Plaza, with construction expected to begin in late July and a projected opening around November 2026. The location will be one of the largest in the brand's portfolio and will include a dedicated conference room for business meetings.

data.location: 19800 MacArthur Boulevard, Suite C10, Irvine, CA
data.short_description: Pacific Pearl Cafe is slated to open a new outpost at 19800 MacArthur Boulevard, Suite C10, in Irvine, according to a recent California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control license filing. Founded by Chef Michael Campbell, the café offers breakfast, lunch, coffee, and baked goods, and currently operates locations in San Juan Capistrano and Costa Mesa.

data.location: 3601 NE Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd, Portland, OR 97212
data.short_description: Syrup Kitchen & Cocktails, a new breakfast and brunch lounge, is set to open this summer at 3601 NE Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd in Portland, according to the brand's Instagram page. The concept is backed by Malcolm Johnson and Fatou Ouattara and will combine a kitchen and cocktail program in a sit-down brunch format.

Lucky Strike is set to replace the Bowlero brand at 6767 Leetsdale Drive in Cherry Creek, Denver, bringing a refreshed look and updated entertainment experience to the bowling venue. Guests can expect state-of-the-art bowling lanes, an upgraded menu, a vibrant arcade, lane-side service, lounge seating, and large-format video walls.

data.location: 55 Tamal Vista Blvd, Corte Madera, CA 94925
data.short_description: Melo's Italian Table, a family-owned Italian restaurant currently operating in Walnut Creek, is slated to open a new location at 55 Tamal Vista Boulevard in Corte Madera, according to a recent California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control license filing. The menu features handcrafted pizzas, house-made pastas, fresh salads, and classic Italian entrées inspired by Southern Italian recipes.

data.status: construction projected to wrap in December 2026
data.short_description: Golden Chick, a Texas-born quick-service chicken chain, is planning to expand to Salado, with the new location being developed by franchisee STN Chicken Group at 2317 Salado Center Loop. The restaurant will span 2,050 square feet, with construction projected to wrap in December 2026; an opening timeline had not been confirmed by publication time.

The team behind local staple Krave Kitchen has filed papers for a new location listed as Krave Social at 2818 Coleman Road, with a certificate of occupancy under review by the Memphis and Shelby County Division of Planning and Development as of June 22. The storefront will provide Krave with 4,200 square feet of space; it is unclear whether the new location will differ significantly from existing Krave Kitchen storefronts.

data.location: 175 Oak Lawn Ave., Suite 102, Dallas, TX 75207
data.short_description: Melodeon Jazz Lounge is planned for 175 Oak Lawn Ave., Suite 102, in Dallas' Design District, with a projected completion around December 2026. The concept, from co-founders Cary Ray and Ricky Derek, will feature ticketed live jazz shows Thursday through Sunday, a kitchen serving Chicago-inspired thin-crust pizza, and a full cocktail program.

Bocce Ristorante, a neighborhood Italian restaurant by Chef Joe Pruner, is set to open at 4801 Folsom Blvd, Suite 2, in East Sacramento, with an expected mid-July opening pending clearance from the city's electrical department. The menu centers on fresh pasta alongside pizzas, sandwiches, and seasonal sides, offered in a fast-casual format with 20-seat indoor dining and a market component.

Los Compadres Cantina, a Tex-Mex concept built around the flavors of Mexico City, is planning a new location in Ponder at 309 N. FM 156, with a projected opening around October 2026. Co-founder Jack Layman cited the area's rapid residential growth as a key factor, and the menu will mirror the existing Los Compadres experience anchored by from-scratch Tex-Mex offerings.

The team plans many additional locations throughout Southeast Michigan, with future shops to be franchised.

data.status: hoping to open the shop by mid-July

The shop will offer specialty espresso drinks, pastries, milkshakes, and a gluten-free and sugar-free menu, transitioning from its origins as an at-home bakery.

The Belmont, a Capitol Hill cocktail bar at 518 E. Pike St., will officially reopen June 25 under new owners Tanakorn Jitmongkonkul and Erin Wilbur, who also own Otter on the Rocks in West Seattle. The revived venue will feature an elevated cocktail program alongside its existing eclectic retro interior, with hours running Tuesday through Sunday.

Zinneken's Belgian Waffles is preparing to open a new outpost at 98A Boylston Street in downtown Boston, just steps from Emerson College and Boston Common. Founder Nhon Ma confirmed the plans but said he is not yet ready to share additional details about the project.

Zinneken's Belgian Waffles is planning a second new location at 28 Amity Street near the University of Massachusetts Amherst. Founder Nhon Ma confirmed the plans but said he is not yet ready to share additional details about the project.

data.short_description: Dick's Drive-In is expanding with an 11th location on the Tulalip Reservation, west of I-5 at Exit 199 and directly across from Quil Ceda Creek Casino, with construction already underway after crews broke ground in June. An official opening date has not been announced.

Port Side, a coffee and breakfast spot in Denver's Five Points neighborhood, has announced its permanent closure after ten years of service, with its last day on Sunday, July 5. Owner Chris Bell stated he decided not to renew the lease, citing the toll business operations have taken on his body.

The Dallas-Fort Worth-born chain is planned for a Braeburn neighborhood opening in southwest Houston. Construction is expected to start this summer and wrap up by end of year, with the location estimated to cost $240,000 for a 2,100 sq ft build-out. The brand is also slated to open a second new location in Rosenberg.
A second new Sal's Nashville Hot Chicken location is slated to open in Rosenberg, Texas, to meet demand for its halal-style hot chicken. No specific address or opening date has been announced.

Ota-Ya, a Japanese restaurant serving sushi, tempura, and traditional dishes for over 31 years in Newtown, PA, is permanently closing on July 3, 2026, after initially planning to close June 28. The owners, Jeff and Cindy Wong, are retiring to spend more time with family, and the property is reportedly planned for redevelopment.

Fogo de Chão is expanding to Crabtree Valley Mall in Raleigh, occupying the former Uncle Julio's 8,438-square-foot space. The Raleigh location is part of the brand's broader North Carolina expansion, which also includes a planned location at The Streets at Southpoint in Durham and a first NC restaurant opening in August at 200 South Tryon Street in Charlotte.

data.short_description: Fogo de Chão has submitted plans for a location at The Streets at Southpoint in Durham as part of its North Carolina expansion. No opening date has been announced.

Nature's Best Cafe, a family-owned scratch-made breakfast and lunch restaurant operating for a decade in Naperville, will permanently close on July 31, 2026. The restaurant announced the closure via Instagram, thanking the community for years of support without citing specific reasons beyond financial challenges referenced in a prior GoFundMe campaign.

Something Good, a neighborhood bar concept from Kansas City owner Greta Gunderson, is planned for 4970 N. Lowell Blvd in Denver, taking over the old Goldspot Brewing space. The bar will offer draft beers, draft cocktails, and a laid-back atmosphere with board games, cozy seating, and no dress code.

Amoret, a new all-day café and cocktail bar from Kurt Henkel and Daniel Masters, is set to open this fall in Denver's RiNo neighborhood at 3100 Brighton Blvd. The concept is designed as a neighborhood gathering place for morning coffee, remote work, lunch, and evening cocktails, inspired by European café aesthetics.

Mozzo owner Shannon Campbell has signed a lease for a fourth Charleston-area location, though the specific address has not yet been announced. The new location will join existing outposts on Coleman Boulevard, in Carolina Park in Mount Pleasant, and downtown Charleston on Meeting Street.

Habaneros, a Pan-Mexican restaurant concept from Louisiana, will open next week on the ground floor of Sora at Spring Quarter in Midtown Atlanta, marking the brand's first Georgia location. The menu blends traditional Mexican dishes with Latin American influences and modern cooking techniques, and includes handcrafted cocktails.

Owner-chef Robb Venditti cited an ADA complaint with potential heavy expenses as a significant factor in the decision to close, along with a desire to spend more time with family.

The owners of HopScotch & Vine announced they would not be reopening at 24047 Lockport Street in Plainfield after 14 years of operation. The closure makes way for Taco Dale Cantina, which has signed on to take over the space.

Taco Dale Cantina is expanding with a second Chicagoland location coming to 24047 Lockport Street in downtown Plainfield, taking over the former HopScotch & Vine space. An opening date has not yet been set for the Mexican restaurant.

Slice Beer Co, a Lincoln-based craft brewery, is expanding to 40 Atlantic Street in Roseville, marking the brand's first location beyond its original Lincoln taproom. Co-founder Russ Yeager confirmed a September opening target; full layout and menu details are still to come.

Talea Beer Co. is opening its sixth location at 441 Amsterdam Ave. on the Upper West Side, an all-day taproom concept offering morning coffee, 16 beers on tap, and breakfast, lunch, and dinner fare. The woman-founded brewery has targeted this neighborhood since opening its Williamsburg location, noting the area's limited bar offerings and demographic alignment with the brand.

The team behind Big O Burgers is opening a new chicken concept called Big O Hot Chicken at 118 N Michigan Avenue in Saginaw, taking over a space previously occupied by Liquid Lounge and Kitchen. Owner Omar Linder stated an opening date will be announced once inspection processes are complete.

data.status: expected to welcome its first guests next month
data.short_description: Let Me Roll It, a new cocktail bar from Ace of Cups owner Conor Stratton and partner Sarah Fleming, is expected to open next month near Italian Village in Weinland Park, Columbus. The 1970s-inspired bar will focus on classic cocktails under $12, canned and bottled beers, and analog music from records and cassettes, with no televisions.

From The Boot is relocating its Lafayette Hill location from 517 Germantown Pike to 400 Germantown Pike at the Shops of Lafayette Hill, after 27 years at the original address. The current location will remain open through July 2, while an opening date for the new spot has not yet been announced.

data.short_description: Zaxby's has signed a second multi-unit development agreement to open seven more restaurants in the Chicagoland area, following the opening of its first Chicago-market location in Plainfield. Specific addresses and opening dates for the new locations have not been announced.

data.location: 517 E Grayson St, San Antonio, TX 78215
data.short_description: Restaurant Claudine, an elevated French-inspired Southern restaurant in San Antonio's Government Hill neighborhood operated by Carpenter Carpenter Hospitality, served its final meal on June 22, 2026, after a four-year run. The hospitality group hinted at future projects, stating "this is not a final goodbye."

Harvest Pizzeria is expanding to downtown Hilliard, taking over the space at 3987 Main St that most recently housed Legacy Smokehouse, which closed last month after nine years. The Hilliard location will be the sixth for Harvest Pizzeria, which launched in German Village in 2011 and is known for wood-fired pizzas made with locally sourced ingredients.

Noble Pizzeria and Barbecue is preparing to close its brick-and-mortar location after nine years of service. Owner Ryan Carey cited a desire to devote more time to his growing family as the reason for the closure. The pizzeria had operated at 476 Stevens Avenue since 2017, offering thin-crust pizzas paired with slow-smoked meats.

Black Rock Coffee Bar plans to open a new location in Parker, Colorado on June 29. The Oregon-based chain's new outlet will be its 19th location in Colorado and 15th in the Denver area. The grand opening week will feature promotions including free drinks, BOGO offers, and limited-edition merchandise.

Paris Baguette has opened a new bakery café in Long Branch, marking its 32nd location in New Jersey. The café is operated by husband-wife franchisees Devanshu and Ameeshi Patel, located at 60 Centennial Drive near Pier Village. The brand is working toward a goal of 1,000 locations across the United States and Canada by 2030.

LB Steak closed its Bishop Ranch location on June 22 as part of Vine Hospitality's closure of all Bay Area restaurant operations. The modern American steakhouse was led by Chef Rolan Passot, a James Beard Award nominee. Vine Hospitality, founded in 1994, stated the business was not successful enough to continue operating.

LB Steak plans to close its Santana Row location on June 24 as part of Vine Hospitality shutting down all operations. The restaurant is a modern American steakhouse with a menu focused on prime cuts and an extensive whiskey and bourbon program. Vine Hospitality owner Alistair Levine stated there are no plans to reopen anything elsewhere in the Bay Area.

Left Bank announced its closure on June 22 on social media as part of Vine Hospitality's shutdown of all Bay Area restaurant operations. Vine Hospitality owner Alistair Levine stated the business was not successful enough to continue and there are no plans to reopen elsewhere.

Petite Left Bank announced its closure on June 22 on social media as part of Vine Hospitality's shutdown of all Bay Area restaurant operations. Vine Hospitality owner Alistair Levine stated the business was not successful enough to continue and there are no plans to reopen elsewhere.

Meso Modern Mediterranean announced its closure on June 22 on social media as part of Vine Hospitality's shutdown of all Bay Area restaurant operations. Vine Hospitality owner Alistair Levine stated the business was not successful enough to continue and there are no plans to reopen elsewhere.

French's Pastry Bakery announced the closing of its Orange location at 2064 N Tustin Street on June 26 due to unavoidable circumstances. The bakery had been operating at the location for 21 years and is known for its signature Wagon Wheel pastry. This is the third French's Pastry Bakery location to close in three years; the original Costa Mesa location will remain open.

data.location: Miracle Mile Shops Next to SAXE Theater, 3663 Las Vegas Blvd S, Las Vegas, NV 89109
data.short_description: TE'AMO Boba & Dessert has opened its newest store at Miracle Mile Shops on the Las Vegas Strip, marking its 25th U.S. location. Founded in 2016 by Mia Wan, the brand specializes in bubble tea, fruit teas, mochi donuts, and cheesecake baos made with organic ingredients. The new Las Vegas store is the brand's first in the market and is part of Miracle Mile Shops' ongoing expansion.

data.location: 675 Ponce De Leon Ave NE, Atlanta, GA 30308
data.short_description: La Cueva, a slot canyon speakeasy and restaurant, opened at Ponce City Market on June 13. The 2,700-square-foot concept was co-founded by Robert Hopper and Peter Terrones, featuring a cave-like atmosphere, Latin-inspired cocktails, and nightly live music and DJs. The beverage program is led by Bar Lead Francis Coligado and Beverage Director Alexander Holender, specializing in pisco and mezcal.

1up Arcade Bar permanently closed its original Blake Street LoDo location on June 22, citing economic challenges. Founded in 2011, the bar offered a full-service bar menu and a large collection of classic arcade games and pinball machines. The team plans to open a new location in the Belmar Shopping District in Lakewood this fall, with other locations on Colfax and in Greenwood Village continuing to operate.

data.store_name: Delightful Deli, Bakery and Sweet Shop
data.short_description: Delightful Deli, Bakery and Sweet Shop will relocate to 3522 Main St., Suite 100A in Rowlett, with the founder expecting to open by August pending permits. The family-owned concept began as a food trailer and is known for signature offerings including chicken salad, housemade cinnamon rolls, and strawberry tres leches cake. The new location plans to expand its lineup with paninis, sub sandwiches on daily-baked bread, and custom drinks.

Ellwood Steak & Fish House is seeking expansion with a new location proposed for 180 W Washington Street in Oswego, at the base of The Reserve at Hudson Crossing apartment complex. Restaurant president Chirag Amin told What Now Chicago he hopes to introduce the new location by October. The project is currently in the proposal review stage and construction has not yet begun.

Based on a City of Las Vegas permit, construction is likely underway and slated to be completed soon, with an anticipated opening this summer. Owner Jianbo Zhang confirmed the opening but was unable to share further details.

Old Town Pizza is set to open inside Roseville's former historic post office at 320 Vernon St., transforming the building into a three-level restaurant and rooftop bar. Founder Reese Browning purchased the building for $1.75 million as part of an $8 million total investment, targeting a late September opening. The rooftop level is designed to seat up to 300 people as a full event and nightlife destination.

Construction is currently underway on the estimated $250,000 project. The new Memorial City location is essentially a relocation of the Bellaire location that closed in March.

Co-owners Ulrika Bengtsson and Sabina Lindmark are behind the concept, which will feature light and fresh fare, a full liquor license, and function as an event venue and community gathering space for the design industry. An opening date is set for the end of July.

The groundbreaking for the site took place on June 15.

The brewery was founded by Chris and Kaitlin McCall in 2020 and currently operates a location in Allentown and a taproom in Breinigsville. The property will not require a major renovation, and brewing operations are planned for the downtown site in addition to the existing Susquehanna Street production facility.

This is the first concept from Adagio Hospitality.

Bayocean Oyster House is set to open at 1985 Bayocean Road NW in Tillamook in spring 2027, restoring a historic oyster processing facility into a working waterside restaurant, seafood market, and processing dock. The menu will center on local oysters, grilled fish, and creative uses for underused coastal species, with a counter-service format designed to keep prices accessible. Chef Jacob Harth is partnering with David Sisler and development firm Urban Patterns on the project.

Flip The Bird permanently closed its Swampscott location, with the closure announcement shared on social media on June 19. The restaurant cited economic challenges including rising construction costs, rent increases, operating expenses, and higher food prices as factors behind the closure. The team stated they are actively looking for a new space near the Swampscott area to reopen, while Beverly and Danvers locations remain open.

Ocean Crab, a new seafood restaurant, is preparing to open at 2935 S Orlando Drive in Sanford, replacing the former WingHouse Bar & Grill. A representative of the restaurant confirmed the opening is expected next month. The restaurant is currently viewable on Google Maps and has already received its first review.

The Washington Square location will be one of the brand's first in the Portland metro area.

Twin Peaks is opening its first-ever Kissimmee location on June 29 at 2911 Vineland Rd, taking over the former Smokey Bones space in the Poinciana Place shopping center. The company invested $4 million in the transformation, resulting in an approximately 8,000-square-foot space with two bars and more than 50 TVs. The new location plans to hire 130 people.

Scooter's Coffee is opening its first location in the Lansing area at 3335 E Michigan Avenue, being debuted by franchisees Michael Endres and Bryan Bender. An opening date has not been released but is expected sometime later this summer. Signage is not yet up at the new location.

Casa Vive, a new yoga studio and wellness space, recently received a permit for a $150,000 build-out at 1520 Prudential Drive in Jacksonville. The project was originally expecting a spring opening, but signs point to it moving forward. The studio is headed up by Lululemon ambassador Alejandra Amegin.

A trailer will operate in front of the unit to preview their offerings ahead of the opening.

data.location: 406 W Belt Line Rd, Cedar Hill, TX 75104
data.short_description: Mija Barbecue, a family-owned barbecue restaurant in Cedar Hill, Texas, announced it will permanently close on June 27, 2026. The owners shared the news on social media, thanking the community for years of support, though no specific reason for the closure was provided. The restaurant began as a backyard barbecue project in 2019 before growing into a brick-and-mortar business in 2024.

Crackin Blue Crabs is an upcoming food truck in the Jacksonville area, discovered through plan review paperwork submitted by Crackin Blue Crabs LLC. The food truck has been active on social media since last year, but co-owner Latasha Armstrong was not immediately available to provide an opening timeline. The brand describes itself as "All Flavor No Flex."

Sheep is a new rooftop dining concept planned for the Clayton Hotel & Members Club in Cherry Creek, Denver, at 233 Clayton Street, set to debut this summer as a three-month residency from July to October. The concept is from Id Est Hospitality Group founder Kelly Whitaker, who co-owns The Wolf's Tailor, Colorado's first two-Michelin-star restaurant. Guests can expect a nightly four-course menu with multiple choices.

McDonald's is preparing to open a new location in Magog on Rue Sherbrooke, across from Walmart, with construction already underway on the vacant site. Franchise owner Caroline Iannuzzi, who operates seven existing McDonald's restaurants in the Estrie region, will oversee the new restaurant. The company confirmed the site is expected to open in Fall 2026.

Gringos Tacos is an upcoming food truck serving Flagler County, with plan review paperwork recently submitted by Dos Bros Foods LLC. The food truck will serve birria tacos and ramen, according to social media posts. Chef Chris Gibbs was not immediately available for comment on the rollout timeline.

Planet Fitness has opened a new 21,141-square-foot fitness center at 3066 228th Avenue SE in Sammamish, its 19th location in the Seattle-Tacoma area. A ribbon-cutting ceremony is scheduled for June 18, 2026, at 2 p.m. The facility includes 83 strength-training machines, 56 cardio machines, a cross-training area, and additional amenities for Black Card members.

Palazzo Pizza Italiana, headed up by Jason Fox and the team at Josephine's Italian Market, is set to open at 214 E Cass St in downtown Tampa this summer. Renderings show a moody interior with a room-length bar and large semi-circular booths. No specific opening date has been set, though the owners hope to welcome guests before the end of summer.
